summary: nordpass npm package: typosquat name with obfuscated postinstall containing joke payload and RE challenge binary
details: Package published as `nordpass` on npm shares its name with the commercial NordPass password manager but is unrelated to that product. The `postinstall` script runs `make -C src && cp src/auth_module./bin/flare && node src/install.js`. `src/install.js` is a ~100KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (hex identifiers, string-array + decoder shape) whose reachable behavior is printing ASCII art. `src/main.c` compiles to a local reverse-engineering challenge binary (FLARE-On-style): it invokes `ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME,...)` as an anti-debug constructor, XOR-decrypts a static `_cfg_blob`, reads a passphrase from stdin via `fgets`, and prints a flag. No outbound network I/O, no reads of installer credentials or environment, no writes outside the package directory, and no dynamic code fetch are present in the reachable code. The concerns are name collision with a well-known product and unexplained heavy obfuscation of a trivially-functional installer script.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
